name: markov_model
description: A state-transition (Markov) diagram: 2–6 health/process states as circles, transition arrows between them (with a probability/rate label), and self-loops for states that also "stay" (optionally captioned with the stay probability). Choose this for ANY request about a Markov model, a health-state transition diagram, or a cycle of states with probabilities of moving between them. All placement is computed for you: a ring for 3+ states or a horizontal row (layout "chain" — the classic textbook style for health-state models), self-loops aimed into each state's least crowded side, and arrows that bow around any state that sits in their way. A state that no transition ever leaves renders as absorbing (plain ink, no color) automatically. `view: "matrix"` draws the transition matrix instead (rows from, columns to, each cell a probability; the stay on the diagonal is derived as 1 − the row's exits and shown grey; up to 10 states — use it from 7 states, or whenever the numbers matter more than the picture); `view: "both"` puts diagram (left) and matrix (right) side by side. Matrix and table are scaled to fill the page (between the heading and the captions); a model too big for the page at readable type (7+ states with trace and compare) is laid out larger than the page — seen whole at rest, read close with `camera: {on: [ids]}` (a row id frames that row). Give it `trace` to RUN the model: a cohort table (counts in each state year by year, QALY weight and cost of each state, the QALYs and cost each year yields, discounted lifetime totals, the average per person, and with `compare` a second option and its cost per QALY gained) — every number computed from the transition labels, so narrate the table's numbers rather than working them out. Beside the diagram the table takes at most 4 states; with the matrix (up to 10) it goes under it with the same columns (or beside it, when that is larger), the matrix then carries each state's QALYs/yr and Cost/yr as columns and, with `compare`, the option's changed values in its colour under the base ones. Per-person QALYs show 2 decimals, and the Difference row is exactly the difference of the rows shown. Drawn text can quote the results live: {markov.qalys_mean}, {markov.cost_mean}, {markov.compare_qalys_mean}, {markov.compare_cost_mean}, {markov.qalys_gained}, {markov.cost_added}, {markov.icer}, {markov.stay_<slug>}, {markov.p_<from>_<to>}.

states.description: 2–10 state names, in the order they should be laid out. The diagram draws at most 6; 7–10 need view "matrix".

transitions.description: Directed transitions between states named in `states`.

self_loops.description: States that also have a "stay" probability — drawn with a small loop aimed into the state's least crowded side. A bare state name, or {state, label} to caption the stay probability.

layout.description: Node arrangement. Default: circle for 3+ states, chain for exactly 2. Pick "chain" explicitly for the classic left-to-right row (e.g. Well → Sick → Dead) — skip-ahead transitions arc around the states between them.

highlight_state.description: One state name (must be in `states`) to highlight with a tinted halo behind it.

trace.description: Run a cohort through the model and draw the table. Transition labels must be probabilities; each state's stay is what its arrows leave. Beside the diagram (view "diagram"): at most 4 states, the diagram moves left. With view "matrix" or "both": the table runs full width under the matrix, up to 10 states, and its QALYs/yr and Cost/yr rows move into the matrix as columns.

start.description: Cohort size, all in the first state (default 1000).

utility.description: QALY weight of a year in each state, in `states` order, e.g. [0.9, 0.5, 0].

cost.description: Cost of a year in each state, in `states` order.

discount.description: Annual discount rate for the totals (default 0.035); year 1 is undiscounted.

compare.description: A second option, e.g. a drug: its name, the transitions it changes (same from/to, new label), and what it adds to a year's cost in each state.

cost.description: What the option adds to a year's cost in each state, in `states` order.

name.description: With `compare`: the first option's name, labelling its per-person row (default "Current care").

view.description: What to draw: "diagram" (default) the states as circles; "matrix" the transition matrix alone (rows from, columns to, derived stay on the diagonal; up to 10 states); "both" the diagram left and the matrix right (with trace, the table under the matrix; keep "both" to 4 states: the diagram gets small).

element_ids.state_<slug>: the ellipse for one state (slug: the state name, lowercased, non-alphanumeric characters replaced with _)
element_ids.state_label_<slug>: the state's name, centered inside its ellipse
element_ids.t_<i>: transition arrow i (0-indexed, in `transitions` order) — bowed automatically when the reverse transition also exists, or to arc around a state that sits in its way
element_ids.t_label_<i>: transition i's probability/rate label, when set
element_ids.loop_<slug>: the self-loop for a state named in `self_loops`
element_ids.loop_label_<slug>: that loop's stay-probability caption, when its `self_loops` entry set a label
element_ids.hl_<slug>: tinted halo behind the state named by `highlight_state` — present only when set
element_ids.title: figure title, when set
element_ids.matrix: with view matrix/both: the whole transition matrix without the compare layer (a set)
element_ids.matrix_cell_<from>_<to>: one cell: the probability of moving from state <from> to <to> (slugs); the diagonal matrix_cell_<s>_<s> is the derived stay, grey on a light wash
element_ids.matrix_row_<slug>: one from-state's row: its name and probabilities — the row that sums to 1 (a set)
element_ids.matrix_values_<slug>: with trace.utility/cost: that row's QALYs/yr and Cost/yr cells (a set)
element_ids.matrix_col_<slug>: one to-state's column: its name and cells (a set)
element_ids.matrix_stay: the diagonal: every derived stay cell (a set)
element_ids.matrix_utility_<slug>: with trace.utility: the state's QALYs/yr cell
element_ids.matrix_cost_<slug>: with trace.cost: the state's Cost/yr cell
element_ids.matrix_head_utility: with trace.utility: the QALYs/yr column head
element_ids.matrix_head_cost: with trace.cost: the Cost/yr column head
element_ids.matrix_corner: the corner cell's diagonal with 'from' and 'to'
element_ids.matrix_rule_head: the rule under the column heads, over the states' columns
element_ids.matrix_rule_from: the rule between the row names and the cells
element_ids.matrix_rule_head_values: with trace.utility/cost: the rule under the QALYs/yr and Cost/yr heads — draw it with them
element_ids.matrix_rule_values: with trace.utility/cost: the rule between the cells and the value columns
element_ids.matrix_values: with trace.utility/cost: both value columns, their heads and rules (a set)
element_ids.matrix_compare_<from>_<to>: with trace.compare: the option's value under a cell it changes (the stay it implies too), in its colour
element_ids.matrix_compare_cost_<slug>: with trace.compare.cost: the option's Cost/yr under the base one
element_ids.matrix_compare_name: with trace.compare: the option's name keying its coloured line, in the first row it changes
element_ids.matrix_compare: the compare layer: every matrix_compare_* value and the name (a set) — draw it after the matrix to show what the option changes
element_ids.trace_head: with trace: the table's header row (the state names, QALYs, Cost)
element_ids.trace_head_rule: with trace: the rule under the header row
element_ids.trace_utility: with trace, view "diagram": the QALY weight of a year in each state (with the matrix, see matrix_utility_<slug>)
element_ids.trace_cost: with trace, view "diagram": the cost of a year in each state (with the matrix, see matrix_cost_<slug>)
element_ids.trace_rule_inputs: with trace, view "diagram": the rule under the QALYs/yr and Cost/yr rows
element_ids.trace_row_<k>: with trace: row 0 the starting cohort; row k (1…cycles) the counts at the end of year k, with that year's QALYs and cost
element_ids.trace_gap: with trace: ⋮ under every column — the years not shown, which the lifetime totals add up
element_ids.trace_rule_total: with trace: the rule above the lifetime totals
element_ids.trace_total: with trace: the cohort's discounted lifetime QALYs and cost
element_ids.trace_discount: with trace: the small "discounted 3.5%" tag beside the lifetime totals
element_ids.trace_mean: with trace: the same per person — the average (labelled with trace.name, default "Current care", when there is a compare)
element_ids.trace_compare: with trace.compare: the second option's average QALYs and cost per person
element_ids.trace_icer_gain: with trace.compare: the Difference row's QALYs gained (compare − first, as shown)
element_ids.trace_icer_cost: with trace.compare: the Difference row's extra cost
element_ids.trace_icer_ratio: with trace.compare: the cost per QALY gained (or "Dominant"/"Dominated")
element_ids.trace_icer: with trace.compare: trace_icer_gain, trace_icer_cost and trace_icer_ratio (a set)

examples.request: Draw a three-state Markov model: Well, Sick, Dead, with Well and Sick able to stay or transition, and Dead absorbing.
Draw the classic Well–Sick–Dead Markov model as a left-to-right row, with stay probabilities on Well and Sick and a direct Well-to-Dead arrow.
Draw a two-state Markov chain for a machine that's either working or broken, with a repair rate and a breakdown rate.
Show a five-state disease model as a transition matrix and run it for a cohort, comparing a new drug that halves progression from mild to severe.
